course_name_original: The legal and economical aspects of entrepreneurship
course_name_en: The legal and economical aspects of entrepreneurship

learning_outcomes.text: This course provides an in-depth exploration of the legal and economic frameworks that govern entrepreneurship. It examines the essential legal principles that affect business formation, operation, and dissolution, as well as the economic theories and practices that influence entrepreneurial ventures. Students will gain a comprehensive understanding of the interplay between legal structures and economic strategies in fostering successful business initiatives.
Identify and analyze the legal structures available for starting a business
Understand the regulatory environment affecting entrepreneurship, including contracts, intellectual property, and employment law
Evaluate the economic factors that influence entrepreneurship, including market analysis, funding sources, and economic indicators

syllabus_topics: Sole proprietorships, partnerships, corporations, and LLCs
Types of intellectual property: patents, trademarks, copyrights
Essential contracts for entrepreneurs (e.g., partnership agreements, service contracts)
Understanding federal, state, and local regulations
Legal and economic aspects of global entrepreneurship
assessment_rules: The condition for passing the course is to achieve all the required learning outcomes specified for the course.
